mentl/02929b2:
float_extract_digits recursed on f * 10.0 against a FIXED exp,
re-deriving scaled = f / pow10(exp - count) each step — so scaled
grew 10^(2*count) unbounded and i32-truncation trapped at the fifth
digit of 1.0. The function computed the correct next value into a
binding named remainder and THREW IT AWAY (the Carried-Truth tell:
the right answer, minted then discarded). Latent since the fn was
written — it had never once executed on a real f64; the seed's
floored floats fed it zeros forever, and tonight's substrate is the
first light it ever saw.

The fix carries the truth instead of re-deriving it: the caller
normalizes ONCE (f / pow10(exp), scaled in [1,10)), each step takes
floor(scaled) as the digit and (scaled - digit) * 10 as the next
scaled, bounded [0,10) for the whole recursion — the bound documented
as load-bearing. Deletes the per-step pow10, the mod-10 double-count,
and the count==0 symptom guard. Probe receipts in-table: clean
0x3FF00000 (1.0) at entry, exactly *10 per level, trap at 1e10.

verify 35 micros green; five integer rungs hold; the +rt rungs no

stdout written during INFERENCE: the ev-slot seam

mentl/027e9ec:
Closes the named follow-up Hβ.emit.nested-fn-idx-globals from H.2.e
landing (commit 38e5a87).

Symptom: `fn main(n) = (x) => x + n` produced (global.get \$8_idx)
and (call_indirect ...) referencing the lambda's fn-idx, but the
$8_idx global was never declared → wat2wasm validation failed
"undefined global variable \$8_idx".

Root cause: $collect_fn_names walked only the top-level lowexprs
list, picking up LLet-wrapped LMakeClosure at depth 0. Nested
LMakeClosures (lambdas inside fn bodies) were emitted by
$emit_functions_walk's recursion, but the funcref table + name_idx
globals didn't see them — so $emit_fn_table_and_globals iterated
only top names.

Fix: $collect_fn_names becomes recursive via $cfn_walk, mirroring
$emit_functions_walk's structure exactly. Walks LLet, LBlock, LIf,
LCall/LTailCall, LBinOp, LMakeVariant, LMakeList, LMakeTuple,
LReturn, LMakeClosure, LMakeContinuation. Every LMakeClosure +
LMakeContinuation appends fn name AND recurses into body.

Verified: `fn main(n) = (x) => x + n` produces:
  (table \$fns 2 funcref)
  (elem \$fns (i32.const 0) \$main \$8)
  (global \$main_idx i32 (i32.const 0))
  (global \$8_idx i32 (i32.const 1))
  ...

spots and kept each hand-rolled the same cache, listener set, read and
write, and notes was about to be the third copy — three places for the
same staleness bug. createLocalStore owns the plumbing once: JSON in
localStorage, a stable snapshot for useSyncExternalStore, per-item
sanitizing so a hand-edited entry can't take the page down, and cache
invalidation on the cross-tab storage event, which none of the copies
handled.

dataset can always be re-downloaded; what she keeps and writes cannot,
and asking at the first decision rather than on load matters because
browsers weigh engagement when granting it.
